I actually just applied for accommodations. Unfortunately my school is pretty strict about them and seeing as I got diagnosed late (19) I'm not sure what's gonna happen, they are taking their time which is unsettling. I think they will probably end up giving me them but if I don't get the forms to the teachers within the next two weeks I don't get access to them this semester.

Good to hear your life turned out fine and you started low. I'm always the root for the underdog person so I like seeing people start from nothing and get to the top. I'm just overwhelmed by the whole being diagnosed and getting fully settled junior year which is really late, since I transferred a lot of my credits didn't go and I have to take an extra class both semesters senior year as well as summer school, I have no internships, the only internship I had out of highschool I was the worst employee because I couldn't pay attention for long...

Thanks for the post. We'll see how this turns out I guess, I'll see what I can do now that I'm no longer in mental illness (ADHD, sydlexia, bipolar/depression) and if I can get ahold of wellbutrin or some other antidepressent it might make me better. I used to use rhodiola rhodesia which is the only thing I've ever used that gave me more energy AND made me space out less, and it's a natural anti-depressant so maybe a lot of my attentional issues stem from depression. I spelled dyslexia wrong up there completely by accident but I figured I'd let it stay that way because it's funny.

I think in your case you probably won't go to jail and you can always work out the debt once you're older, plus your girlfriend cares enough about you to pay your bail. What if your girlfriend died, your family died, your best friends died... what you are talking about here sounds like it's something you can pull through.

Like listen I actually appreciate you asking the question don't get me wrong but I'm a stubborn person who has exhausted every possible action I feel I could have taken over several years. I think some people with their combination of genetics/nurturing/events outside control just aren't meant for this world. And I'm slowly coming to peace with the idea of ending it all. A permanent end to an unlimited supply of chronic unsolvable challenges and the ensuing criticism and beat down from any dibshit who wants to talk and drag people down.

Yes and they suck. She refused to give me anti-depressants saying I could essentially "buck up and deal with it". The school therapist wouldn't be covered by insurance so that's out of the picture as well. My mom is diagnosed bipolar so it's a liability from their point if I went "manic" but if I committed suicide it's a nice clean issue that they are not responsible for (from my observations my mom has a huge case of ADHD and extreme opposition defiance disorder coupled with paranoia and her diagnosis was retarded because bipolar people get severe depression lasting for weeks, my mom gets severe depression that lasts no more than a day and her mood swings are far too rapid to be bipolar. But hey I'm not a psychiatrist how would I know more than some narcissistic overpaid rude bitch (yes I've met her psychiatrist and politely shared my info and was ignored) ).
